title.zh: 果蠅男人大腦全圖：性徵如何編織出不同的神經電路？
title.en: The Male Fly Brain Unwrapped: How Sex Shapes Neural Circuits

summary.zh:
【總結】這項研究完成了果蠅雄性中樞神經系統的第一份完整連接體，包含166,700個神經元與11,710種神經元類型，並首次以突觸級解析度對照雄性和雌性大腦。研究發現，雖然性二型性神經元僅佔雄性中樞腦的約4.8%、雌性約2.4%，但它們高度集中於高級腦區，而非感覺與運動的外圍區域。雄性特有的連接被組織成由雄性神經元或樹突定義的「熱點」，而二型性神經元則在不同性別間重新路由資訊。這項成果為理解基因如何塑造行為迴路提供了前所未有的完整視圖。

【研究問題】過去對果蠅性二型行為（如求偶與攻擊）的研究，大多聚焦於單一神經元類型的影響，卻缺乏從基因到完整迴路的系統性視角。雖然已知fruitless（fru）和doublesex（dsx）轉錄因子能標記二型性神經元，但它們如何組裝成功能迴路仍不清楚。此外，此前已有的雌性大腦連接體與雄性神經索連接體彼此孤立，無法進行跨性別的全腦比較。解開這個問題，將有助於理解大腦如何將相同的基本傳感器與運動元件，組裝成截然不同的行為輸出。

【研究方法】研究團隊使用7台增強型聚焦離子束掃描電子顯微鏡（eFIB-SEM），歷經13個月掃描，產生了160太拉體素的8奈米等向解析度影像，涵蓋中央大腦、視葉與腹神經索。透過洪水填充網路自動分割神經元，再以人工校對（proofreading）確保精確性，共檢測到4,600萬個突觸前與3.12億個突觸後位點（精確率/召回率各0.82/0.81）。研究將該雄性連接體與現有的雌性大腦連接體（FAFB/FlyWire）進行空間變換與NBLAST形態比對、連接共聚類等方法進行配對，並標註fru與dsx表現，最終識別出11,710種神經元類型，並進行全腦感覺─運動資訊流的maxflow分析。

【結果】研究團隊鑑定出8,069種同構（isomorphic）、138種二型性、289種雄性特有、71種雌性特有的神經元類型。性二型性與性別特有神經元高度集中於高級腦區：中央腦中分別佔雄性神經元的1.4%與3.4%、雌性1.4%與1%，但視葉與感覺神經元幾乎完全同構。在視覺系統中，研究發現一個雄性特有的「愛-spot」迴路：視神經元LoVP92在雄性中接收來自雄性特有中間神經元的輸入，並透過VES200m抑制轉向指令神經元DNg13，從而調節求偶相關的轉向行為。在聽覺系統中，研究描繪出一個控制求偶歌曲檢測與產生的反覆回饋迴路，其中雄性特有的下行神經元（pMP2、pIP10）驅動歌曲產生，而上行神經元（AN08B074、AN08B084）則將歌曲產生迴路與歌曲檢測中枢相連。化學感覺系統中，費洛蒙反應的神經元也顯著偏向二型性連接。這些發現揭示：即使只有少數神經元具有性別差異，它們仍能透過廣泛的連接影響全腦資訊流，為理解性二型行為的神經架構奠定了系統性基礎。
summary.en:
**Summary:** This study presents the first complete connectome of the adult Drosophila male central nervous system, mapping 166,700 neurons across 11,710 cell types, and provides the first brain-wide, synapse-resolution comparison between male and female flies. Although sexually dimorphic neurons comprise only about 4.8% of male and 2.4% of female central brain neurons, they are heavily concentrated in higher-order brain centers rather than sensory or motor periphery. Male-specific connections form hotspots defined by male-specific neurons or arbors, while dimorphic neurons reroute information across sexes. This resource offers an unprecedented whole-brain view of how genes sculpt behavioral circuits.

**Problem:** Previous studies on Drosophila sexual dimorphism—such as courtship and aggression—have largely focused on the effects of individual cell types, lacking a systematic, circuit-level perspective from genes to behavior. While the transcription factors fruitless (fru) and doublesex (dsx) are known to mark dimorphic neurons, how these neurons assemble into functional circuits remains poorly understood. Moreover, existing connectomes were sex-specific: a female brain and a male nerve cord, but never both in the same animal or compared directly. Solving this gap is crucial to understanding how the brain reorganizes shared sensory and motor hardware to produce sex-specific behaviors.

**Approach:** The team used seven enhanced focused ion beam scanning electron microscopes (eFIB-SEM) over 13 months to generate a 160-teravoxel, 8-nanometer isotropic-resolution volume spanning the central brain, optic lobes, and ventral nerve cord. Neurons were automatically segmented with flood-filling networks, producing 46 million presynaptic and 312 million postsynaptic sites (precision/recall: 0.82/0.81), then manually proofread. The male connectome was matched to the existing female FAFB/FlyWire dataset using spatial transforms, NBLAST morphological comparison, and connectivity co-clustering. Neurons were annotated for fru and dsx expression, typed into 11,710 categories, and analyzed for whole-brain sensory-to-motor information flow using maxflow analysis.

**Results:** The researchers identified 8,069 isomorphic, 138 dimorphic, 289 male-specific, and 71 female-specific neuron types. Dimorphic and sex-specific neurons are concentrated in higher brain centers: 1.4% and 3.4% of male central brain neurons, and 1.4% and 1% of female central brain neurons, respectively, while optic lobes and sensory neurons are nearly entirely isomorphic. In the visual system, the team discovered a male-specific love-spot circuit: the visual neuron LoVP92 receives input from a male-specific interneuron and, through VES200m, inhibits the turning-command neuron DNg13, thereby modulating courtship-related turning behavior. In the auditory system, a recurrent feedback loop was mapped that controls courtship song detection and production, with male-specific descending neurons (pMP2, pIP10) driving song and ascending neurons (AN08B074, AN08B084) linking song production circuits back to central detection centers. In chemosensory systems, pheromone-responsive neurons showed strong bias toward dimorphic connectivity. These findings reveal that even a small fraction of sex-differentiated neurons can exert brain-wide influence through extensive connectivity, laying a systematic foundation for understanding the neural architecture of sexual dimorphism.

keyArticle.title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
